 AGC's bid to seek court ruling no reason to keep Najib in Kajang Prison, say lawyers
 By TARRENCE TAN 
 Saturday, 07 Nov 2026
 | 4:20 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark

 World 
 30 Oct 2026

 Nation 
 22h ago

 Thailand 
 1h ago

 PETALING JAYA: The Attorney General's Chambers' (AGC) bid for an urgent court ruling is no reason to keep Datuk Seri Najib Razak in Kajang Prison, says lawyer Kitson Foong.
 He said the AGC was right to take legal questions to court but only a court could stay or change the High Court's order for house arrest.
 "Who decides where Najib sleeps tonight? Not the AG. Until and unless a court does so, that order should be carried out," he said.
 The AGC said on Friday (Nov 6) that Najib's house arrest should be put on hold and that he remain at his existing place of detention pending clarification.
 On Saturday (Nov 7), the AGC said it was not disputing the pardon but wanted an urgent court ruling on whether the discharge order meant Najib's jail sentence in the SRC International case had ended, and if so, whether his 15-year jail sentence in the 1MDB case, which was to commence after completing the SRC International case sentence, should begin.
 It said a court ruling would also protect Najib's rights as he could still be imprisoned even if that sentence had ended.
 Foong said this was a fair point but it does not justify keeping Najib in Kajang Prison as he was still a prisoner either way, as his Jalan Langgak Duta home was gazetted as a prison on Friday.
 "Nothing is lost by complying. A prisoner who is moved between two prisons can always be moved back.
 "But days spent in Kajang Prison that the court order did not call for cannot be given back," he said.
 He said the answer was plain as the order discharging Najib also stated that he would serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
 "In my opinion, a court that knows Najib was given both jail and a fine would not wipe out the jail term with a fine receipt," he said.
 Foong said the pardon likewise allowed Najib to serve the "remainder of his sentence" at home.
 "One cannot serve the 'remainder' of a sentence that has already ended," he said.
 Lawyer Mohamed Haniff Khatri Abdulla, in an interview on Friday night, said Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar sat on the Pardons Board that decided on Najib's pardon and also heads the 1MDB prosecution team.
 "He already knew about the 1MDB case sentence since Dec 26, before the Pardons Board met.
 "Whatever questions arise on the effect of the pardon, he should have studied them at that time," he said.
 Haniff also pointed to Mohd Dusuki's remarks on Nov 1, when he told reporters that Najib would stay in prison as long as the fine remained unpaid.
 "Why didn't you say then that even if Najib paid the RM50mil, you would need to study it after?
 "To me, this is not about Najib Razak – this is an issue of the rule of law," he added.
 Istana Negara said on Saturday that the pardon was clear and not linked to any other case and that with all its conditions fulfilled, disputing it verged on defying the King's decree.
 The AGC, in its statement, denied that the Attorney General had exceeded his authority or caused Najib to be unlawfully detained.
 Najib remains in Kajang Prison on Saturday, with his house arrest still on hold.
